requirements.requirement: Run a containerized web application on node1 as the unprivileged appsvc account, serving on port 8080
requirements.summary: cmd-082ec6ff8c6f49a0 shows webapp.service active/running a rootless podman container (httpd:alpine) as appsvc (uid 1000), port 8080 listening via pasta, and curl returning HTTP_STATUS:200. Confirmed again post-reboot in cmd-c5c004cf0c4045f9 and cross-checked by the fixed after_executor listening-sockets snapshot showing '*:8080' owned by pasta.avx2.

requirements.requirement: Application starts at boot while the appsvc account has no active login session
requirements.summary: Full bounded transition is directly observed: pre-restart baseline (cmd-e55f9e5990174335) shows webapp.service active+enabled, Linger=yes, boot_id 06339ff3...; a real reboot was acknowledged (cmd-25af71eac79747aa) and directly demonstrated by node unreachability (cmd-3904124f84d74939, cmd-f4efe1a852f243cd) followed by reconnection with a new boot_id 997baa55... (cmd-85f008615ba5410a, cross-checked by global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity); post-restart recovery (cmd-c5c004cf0c4045f9) shows webapp.service auto-started and enabled, only a linger-spawned 'manager' class session present for appsvc (no tty/pts session), port 8080 listening, and HTTP 200 on both loopback and node IP.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence: a rootless podman container run as appsvc serves HTTP 200 on port 8080, and a real single-node reboot (boot_id changed from 06339ff3... to 997baa55...) directly demonstrated the service auto-starting at boot with only a linger-spawned session (no active login) for appsvc, both before and after the transition. Executor command sequencing was efficient; the one failed sub-step (machinectl shell) was promptly corrected without leaving broken state, and only trivial log residue remains.
limitations: Evidence for 'no active login session' relies on loginctl session class reporting rather than an independent audit source; this is standard but not cross-verified by a second mechanism.
The dnf-install.log residue in /tmp was not explicitly assessed by the executor for cleanup, though it is low-risk and expected from a package installation.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to task prerequisites or evidence collection: installing podman, creating appsvc with subuid/subgid, enabling linger, writing the systemd --user unit, and enabling/starting the service (cmd-ea0ab94bdc5d47c0, cmd-082ec6ff8c6f49a0) were all necessary. The first attempt to start the service via 'machinectl shell' in cmd-ea0ab94bdc5d47c0 failed (machinectl not found) and left the unit disabled/inactive, but this was corrected in the very next command (cmd-082ec6ff8c6f49a0) using the appsvc D-Bus user bus directly, a legitimate corrective action rather than an unnecessary mutation. The scheduled reboot (cmd-25af71eac79747aa) was required to produce the restart evidence. Minor residue: /tmp/dnf-install.log was left behind by the podman install (visible in the after_executor temporary-files diff) — low-risk, non-destructive log residue, not cleaned up. No failed services, no conflicting units, and no unsafe exposure are present in the after_executor snapshot.
